newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Severn on target to cut leaks.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Severn on target to cut leaks.

text.p: British water and sewerage company Severn Trent Plc is on track to achieve targets for cutting leakage to 12 percent of supplies by 2000, chief executive Vic Cocker told Reuters in a telephone interview.

"We're committed to achieving 12 percent by 2000 and we're already at 16, a year ahead of...targets that were agreed with (industry regulator) Ofwat, so we feel we're well on track to achieve what has been promised," Cocker said.
The new Labour government said it would introduce mandatory targets for companies to cut leaks as part of a 10-point plan launched at a crisis summit in mid-May aimed at tackling the current drought.
Cocker said Severn Trent was now providing a free service to repair leaks on customer pipes, a recommendation in the 10-point plan, instead of a subsidised service which it had previously.
Severn Trent has also set up a two million stg charitable fund to help customers who have problems paying their bills.
Cocker said Severn Trent had made a submission to the government on plans to introduce a one-off tax on the excess profits of privatised utilities in a first budget on July 2.

"We have emphasised the need to think in the long term about the need for investment in the industry...and the need to take into account those companies who, like us, have made rebates (to customers)," he said.
